claim: This type is a chain of four fixed filter sections and an output gain: a low shelf, two peaking sections that share one law, a high shelf. The low shelf is one pole and one zero, and so is the high one -- which the band profiles this was read from could not say, because they are magnitude and a second-order section differs from a first-order one in phase everywhere and in magnitude only past a corner this unit has no output beyond. Each parameter byte selects from a short table rather than driving a formula -- a gain answers over twenty-five values and sticks at both ends, a corner has two states, a width has five entries and returns the first for anything past them, a centre moves in equal steps of log frequency for every eighth value of its byte, at the named third octaves between the printed ends and at one entry that is not one of them.
why_not_named: Naming it would add nothing the claim does not already say and would carry a topology this run did not test. The high shelf's order is open, and a name would close it by implication.

era_priors.claim: A parameter byte indexes a coefficient table rather than driving a formula.
era_priors.why: Computing a filter coefficient from a byte needs transcendental functions a fixed-point part of that period does not have, and a table of a few tens of entries costs it nothing.
era_priors.would_be_wrong_if: A parameter answered differently at every one of its 128 values with no repeats. Four of this type's eleven bytes repeat: the widths have five entries, the corners two, the centres one per eight values, and the gains one per value over a window of twenty-five.

era_priors.claim: The chain runs below the converter's rate, so its response ends at that rate's half.
era_priors.why: Effect processing shared a slower clock than the output in this generation of part.
era_priors.would_be_wrong_if: The unit answered above the half rate the model assumes. It does not: the output stands 31.9 dB over silence at 16 kHz, 16.3 at 17 and nothing at 18.

adds: The archive says what each byte did to each band. It does not say that those profiles are the response of a cascade of second-order sections, that the low shelf is one pole rather than two, or that the two mids are one law rather than two that happen to agree at the three settings both were asked at. Each of those is a structure fitted to the readings, and the fit is what this file holds.

alternatives.reading: The high shelf is one pole and one zero, as the low one is.

separated_by.observable: The high shelf's profile where it levels off.

predicts.first order: About 3.6 dB per octave through the corner.

separated_by.sensitivity_here: The slope is published at two resolutions and they agree for the low shelf (3.5 to 3.7) and disagree for the high one (7.1 against 9.8), which is what a profile still climbing at the edge of the set does.
separated_by.why_not_separable: Superseded, and kept because the reason it gave is worth reading against what happened. It was right that the profile does not level off before this unit's output ends and right that no stimulus can be put past it. Its last sentence -- that no further reading of these takes would separate the two -- was written when the only reading there was read band energy, and it did not hold: the takes had phase in them all along.

alternatives.taken_up_by: A residual against the wave rather than against a band profile, on three voices this model was never fitted on. Each order was given the corner and the gain that suited it -- 11257.3 Hz for one pole and one zero, 7753.3 Hz for the unit-slope second-order section -- because a candidate beaten while wearing the winner's parameters has not been beaten. One pole and one zero wins on every voice and every setting, by 2.68 dB at the narrowest and 22.23 at the widest, and it reaches the floor the setting's own two takes set on five of the nine while the second-order section never comes within 3.69 dB of it. The observable this entry said was needed -- the profile past its corner -- is still out of reach, and it was not what decided it: a second-order section has twice the phase slope of a first-order one, and phase accumulates below a corner as well as above it, so a reading that carries phase does not have to see past the corner to tell them apart.

alternatives.reading: The low shelf is a second-order shelving section.
alternatives.ruled_out_by: Its residual leans across the bands of the low corner's record where the first-order one does not, and the low shelf's profile did settle inside the band set, so the lean is the model's and not the reading's. The two candidates that put a second-order section at the low end are the only two of the five that lean on a record whose profile the bands contained.

alternatives.reading: The width byte selects the Q values the manual prints against it.
alternatives.ruled_out_by: It leans on 11 of the 22 records that carry an effect, against none for the winner, and its residual is the largest of the eight candidates on every record that carries one. Since this was first written the width byte has a class of its own and the printed figures were scored against every record of this type that sweeps one: they give seven times the winner's residual there and are refuted by the width the unit puts over half its peak, which is forty-nine bands where the printed figures render thirty.

alternatives.reading: The third entry of the centre table is a third octave like the other fifteen, and what the runs read there is something about the reading rather than about the table.
alternatives.ruled_out_by: The chain carrying 315 Hz there breaks down at the setting that selects it -- 6.57 dB, a share of 0.527 of that record's span -- and every record whose residual leans is a record that sweeps across it. The chain carrying 279 does neither, and the two differ in nothing else. The entry is two bands of this reading below the series against the half band it resolves, five settings across the type's two mid addresses return it, and the same section inside two combination types returns it as well. What is not settled is why, and that is a different sentence.

the_cut_that_is_not_the_boost.what: A peaking section's cut is not its boost inverted. Read at all twenty-five of one section's gain settings rather than at three, the mirrored pair at nine decibels comes back 0.46 dB apart at the widest width and 0.14 at the width one along, where three other pairs are inside a quarter of a decibel at both. Every model in this catalogue renders a peaking section whose cut is the exact mirror of its boost, so none of them has this.
the_cut_that_is_not_the_boost.not_on_the_shelves: The same asymmetry is absent from the shelf pair, whose cut is its boost negated to a median 0.02 dB over twenty-two bands on another type. So this is the peaking sections and not the chain.
the_cut_that_is_not_the_boost.why_it_is_here_and_not_in_the_gain_class: The byte is a decibel a step on both halves; what differs is what the section does with the number. That is this type's topology, and the gain class says so and hands it back.
the_cut_that_is_not_the_boost.what_would_settle_it: The same mirrored pairs at the three widths not yet asked, and on a centre away from the middle of the band set. Whether the asymmetry is a constant, a function of the width, or a rounding is not read yet, and the pairs that are inside a quarter of a decibel bound it to something small over most of the byte.

compared_against.generated_from: data/units/roland-sc8850-01/index.json, every efx-bands record filed under type 01 00 at the twelfth-octave resolution

excluded.why: The same takes read at the coarser set. Scoring both resolutions counts one measurement twice and weights the rows that have two records over the rows that have one.

stimulus: channel 2, program 126, note 60, velocity 100, held 8.0 s, captured 9.0 s
domain.outside: Nothing above 16 kHz, where the unit's output ends and the model's own rate runs out. The band records behind every figure above were taken one byte at a time and on one stimulus, so what they show is each section right on its own, on one voice, in magnitude. Two of those three limits have since been read past in the wave domain and the reading is beside this one; the third has not, and no stimulus this unit can be given reaches above its own output.

residual.unit: share of the span the effect commands in that record
residual.why: Of the 35 records scored, 1 has a residual that leans across its settings or its bands by more than the run's own floor, and it is a width record whose reading does not level off inside the band set. Two leant when this was first published and the second was the high corner's own record, put down then to the bound that corner was transcribed from. It was not that: the renderer was putting a first-order shelf's half-gain point in the wrong place near the model's own Nyquist, and with that corrected the record stops leaning and its worst point falls from 4.74 dB to 1.08 over a span of 12.79.

breaks_down_at.why: Nothing. No setting's residual reaches half the span its record commands. The three points that used to stand here were the two mid centres fitted rather than identified, and they went when the round below put the identified tables in -- this field went on naming them afterwards and no longer does.
breaks_down_at.what_it_does_not_reach: The gain rows. Twenty-five settings of one peaking section's gain were added to this set and none of them leans under this reading, so what the chain has wrong is where a centre sits and not what a gain is worth.

gross.why: The median residual over the span the effect commands, taken as the worst of the records scored. A rejection bound and not a target: below it the residual is reported and never optimised, because no candidate is decided by it.

qualitative.why: Properties the unit's readings have that the model's readings must have too. No arithmetic over a residual rescues a model that cuts where the unit boosts.

power.beaten_by: leaning where the winner does not
power.why: The runner-up in the catalogue, scored on the same records, and whether it leans or contradicts a property where the winner does neither. The decoy is not chosen -- it is whichever candidate came second, so a strawman cannot be put up in its place. A class holding one candidate is a catalogue that is unfinished, which is a finding and not a pass.

records_the_run_did_not_reach.why: The profile had not levelled off where the band set ended, so the corner the model takes from this record is a lower bound. A residual leaning across the bands is that bound leaning. Answering it needs a stimulus that reaches further, not a different model.

The profile had not levelled off where the band set ended, so the corner the model takes from this record is a lower bound. A residual leaning across the bands is that bound leaning. Answering it needs a stimulus that reaches further, not a different model.

breakdown.why: A point worse than 0.5 of the span is a failure at that point rather than error at it. A residual that leans with the setting or with frequency is pointing at a structure the model does not have; one that does not is pointing at the room and the converters, and is not made smaller by anything this project can do.

refuted_by: A setting of any of the eleven bytes whose band profile the chain cannot produce at all -- a second peak, an asymmetric one, a corner that moves with the gain applied through it. Or a byte turning out to answer at values the tables here say are repeats: the widths at 5 and above, the centres between multiples of eight, the gains outside 52 to 76.
what_this_does_not_settle: Which of the two printed labels goes with which state of a corner byte. A label is not measurable.
Whether the same eleven bytes behave this way on any other unit, or under the MSB 04 composite types that print the same rows.

Why one entry of the centre table is not a third octave. The chain reproduces with it and breaks down without it, on five settings across two addresses and on two more types, so it is the unit's and not the reading's. What produced it is not read here and this model carries it as a figure rather than as a law.

Whether the high shelf's asymptotic gain is the twelve decibels its byte's window names. The wave puts its corner and its order beyond doubt and the asymptote is past where this unit has output, so what is read there is the section's shape below it and not its far end.

Whether the mid sections are as right as the shelves. They are the one part the wave leaves above the floor -- ten to twelve decibels on two voices, where the shelves reach it -- and nothing here says whether that is the section, the path its gain reaches it by, or the takes.

the_round_that_took_the_identified_table.what_moved: The two mid centres and the two mid widths. They were curves fitted to this type's own records and they are now the tables their own parameter classes identified: the named third octaves between the printed ends indexed by the byte's top four bits, and the five printed widths halved. Nothing else in the chain changed -- the shelves, the gain window, the corner states and the output level are the same numbers as before.
the_round_that_took_the_identified_table.why_it_was_not_done_earlier: Neither byte had a class when this type was first scored. A readout is what a model may carry while its quantity is unidentified, and it was published as one rather than dressed as a law. What a readout cannot do is come out wrong, which is why the fitted numbers passed every gate they could fail while sitting a sixth of an octave from the table at the bottom of the range.

broke_down_at.now: gone at the setting it was read at, and the same record broke down instead at the setting that selects the entry the series misses

what_it_cost_before.read_as: Two of the three worst points were the fitted centre and not the chain. The fit that produced them is pulled towards the longer flank of a peak and the peaks at the bottom of the table are two octaves wide, so the error was largest exactly where the table is easiest to check -- and it was invisible while the model and the record carried the same number.

what_the_one_entry_buys.read_as: The two chains differ in one number out of every number in them: the third entry of the centre table, 279.1 Hz against the named third octave's 315. The residual barely moves -- that entry is eight of a hundred and twenty-eight settings -- and the breakdown gate turns over, because every record whose residual leaned is a record that sweeps across that entry. A residual meaned over a type is nearly blind to one entry of one table, and the gate that is not is the one that decides.
what_the_one_entry_buys.and_what_it_does_not_buy: It does not make the entry understood. Fifteen entries of this table could have come out wrong and did not; the sixteenth is read off a record and could not have. The frequency class holds it open and publishes it as a readout, and this chain carries the readout with the entry named rather than folding it into the series and calling the series right.

the_decoy_this_time.beaten_by: leaning where the winner does not
the_decoy_this_time.why_it_is_the_right_one: The runner-up is this same chain without the one entry, which is the strongest competitor there is: it is not a different reading of the type, it is the reading with the one thing this round added taken back out. A decoy that differed in the shelves or in the widths would have been beaten on something this round did not change.

how_a_gain_reaches_these_sections.what: The model this claim was scored against builds each of its four sections at the gain its byte names, and for all four of them that is now measured to be wrong everywhere except at the ends of the window and at its centre. Each byte blends one stored full-scale section against the dry path. Which end the stored section sits at is not the same for the two kinds of section, which is why there are two claims and not one.

settled_in.the high shelf: Neither. Its own records hold three settings and two of them are the window's ends, where every reading of a gain path is the same section.

how_a_gain_reaches_these_sections.why_this_claim_does_not_move: Nothing this claim says is contradicted. It says the type is a chain of four sections and an output gain and that each byte indexes a short table, and all of that stands; what the other claim identifies is the path between one of those tables and the section it feeds. The two were separable only because this claim's own records were read again with a different instrument -- the width of the feature rather than the residual over the profile -- and this claim's verdict is what the residual said, which is still what it said.
how_a_gain_reaches_these_sections.what_a_reader_rendering_this_type_should: This chain for the topology, the tables and the corners, and the two claims beside it for what the gain bytes do with them -- the mid sections blending towards a section stored at full boost, the shelves towards one stored at full cut, and the far side of each byte that same section turned over. Taking this model alone reproduces the ends of every gain's range, makes both mid peaks too wide in between, and puts both shelves' transitions about half an octave out in the other direction.
how_a_gain_reaches_these_sections.why_it_was_not_caught_here: Three gates passed on it for two rounds, on these records. A residual meaned over a record is nearly blind to it, because the settings where the paths differ are the ones whose profile is smallest and so carry the least of the record's span; and the lean test looks for a residual running with the setting or with frequency, while this one is a hump that is nothing at both ends of the window and nothing at its centre. The gate that would have caught it is the qualitative one, and nothing had stated the property for it to hold. On the shelves it was missed twice over: the first reading put to them was a peak's, and under it they refused a blend they are in fact doing.

the_width_byte_read_at_two_more_centres.what: Four records of `40 03 08` entered this claim's comparison set without being chosen for it: a run swept the byte at all five entries at two centres the width class needed, and the set is generated from the index rather than listed by hand. They are the first records of this type taken with the centre byte anywhere but the two ends of its table.
the_width_byte_read_at_two_more_centres.why_it_is_not_a_round: The model file does not move and the claim does not move. Four records of a byte already in the domain were added to a set the claim regenerates, and the same chain answers them at the same residual. What a round is for is a chain that had to change.
the_width_byte_read_at_two_more_centres.what_it_adds: The two mid centres were only ever read at the ends of their own table in this set, and a table read at its ends is a table two points constrain. These sit at its fourth and thirteenth entries, and the chain renders both within the same residual it renders everything else at -- so the sixteen-entry table is answering inside its range and not just across it.

what_the_wave_said.what: The model applied to a flat take as a complex response, aligned to a take of the swept setting to a fraction of a sample, level fitted and subtracted. The residual carries the phase, which a band profile does not have.

on_what.held_out: Three voices the model was never fitted on. Every band record behind it was taken on one stimulus, which is program 126 held eight seconds.
on_what.why_these: Struck, and through a type with no modulator. A note-on does not reset a modulator, so a take through one does not repeat and neither would any model of it -- this unit's own repeat stage reads a struck note at 55 dB down through a static effect and at 59 dB above its floor through a modulated one. The eight-second voice the band records use does not repeat either: two of its takes, aligned and level fitted against each other, leave a tenth of a decibel below the take.

what_the_wave_said.the_floor_each_reading_is_against: The setting's own two takes subtracted from each other. Its own rather than the flat ones, because a residual is reported against what it is a residual of: read against the flat take, a setting eight decibels louder comes back eight decibels better for having been louder.

what_the_phase_was_worth_db.what: The same subtraction with the response stripped to its magnitude, which is the most a band reading could ever have constrained, less the residual with the phase in it. Nobody offers the magnitude-only chain as a candidate: the gap is the part of this comparison the published readings could not have made.

what_the_wave_said.the_sections_combine: `allfour` is the low shelf, the high shelf and both mids away from their centres together, which no band record asked. It lands -0.72 dB from the floor on the glockenspiel and 8.1 on the piano, against -5.7 dB for doing nothing. The chain's sections were shown to be right one at a time; this is them together.

what_the_renderer_was_doing.what: `_first_order_shelf` documents its corner as the half-gain point, which is where this archive's `half_below_hz` and `half_above_hz` are read, and it prewarped the frequency the analogue prototype puts a factor of the root of the gain away rather than the corner itself. Below a tenth of the rate the two agree to thousandths.
what_the_renderer_was_doing.why_the_band_gates_did_not_see_it: The low shelf sits at a hundredth of the model's rate and was exact there, which is why the low corner reproduced throughout. The high shelf's own record says its deviation was still climbing where the band set ended, so there was little up there for a residual to fail on, and what did fail read as the lean of a bound. The cookbook second-order shelf next door was exact at every corner, so the two orders were being compared on unequal terms -- which is the comparison this claim's standing alternative was about.
what_the_renderer_was_doing.what_else_it_reaches: Every model in the archive with a first-order shelf near its own Nyquist. Of the records behind this claim's class 3 of 35 can move, because the rest hold the high shelf's gain at the centre of its range where the section is unity whatever its corner. The gain class moves 2 of 9 and the shelf-gain class 2 of 4; the frequency, width and section-gain classes move none.

the_high_corner_is_a_value_now.what: Each candidate corner applied to a flat take and scored by the same waveform residual, over a grid of forty-five corners and seventeen gains. The cut and the boost are two readings of one section and they now agree.
the_high_corner_is_a_value_now.before_the_renderer_was_fixed: The same search put the cut's corner at the top of its grid and the boost's at seven kilohertz -- one section answering two settings with corners a factor of two apart, which is what sent this back to the renderer.

the_control.what: The low shelf searched the same way and first. A search that does not return a corner the claim already has on a section the wave residual says is right is a search reading itself.

why_this_is_not_a_round: `rounds` counts revisions of a claim's model, and this model file is unchanged: the same four sections, the same corners, the same tables and the same orders. What was revised is the code that renders it and the set of things the archive can read, and the alternative the wave settled is this claim's own reading of the high shelf rather than a rival to it -- taking it up swaps no model for another. The claim is at its ceiling of three and parking it here would file a claim that has just lost its last open reading as one still waiting on something.
